newsitem.title: USA: EPA announces latest round of "brownfields" grants.
newsitem.headline: EPA announces latest round of "brownfields" grants.

text.p: U.S. EPA Administrator Carol Browner announced the Clinton Administration is adding 16 new pilot projects totaling $2.06 million in 12 states to help clean up and redevelop "brownfields."

Brownfields are abandoned, lightly polluted commercial properties that lie idle in cities. They are not contaminated enough to qualify for cleanup under the Superfund program administered by the Environmental Protection Agency.
EPA said the 16 cities get two-year grants totaling between $90,000 to $200,000 as seed money to "leverage" other public and private funds to attract economic activity.
The administration has funded 76 pilot projects since it announced its Brownfields Initiative in November 1993, EPA said.

The new pilot projects include: $90,000 for Concord, N.H.; $90,000 for Naugatuck Valley, Conn.; 120,000 for New Haven, Conn.; $90,000 for Portland, Maine; $100,000 for Somerville, Mass.; $200,000 for Cincinnati, Ohio; $200,000 for a consortium of communities in the Dearborn, Mich., suburbs; $100,000 for Kalamazoo, Mich.; $200,000 for Milwaukee County, Wisc.; $100,000 for Bonne Terre, Mo.; $100,000 for Oakland, Calif.; $100,000 for Port of Bellingham, Wash.; $100,000 for Silver Valley, Idaho; and $100,000 for the Puyallup Tribe in Tacoma, Wash.
For more information, call RCRA/Superfund Hotline at 1-800-424-9346.
